markdown_report:
The selected experiment adds a causal recent-summary gate to the corrected NextItNet residual blocks. It targets stale-history persistence and broadly relevant recommendations that miss current purpose, while testing Electronics’ weak lower-tail separation. Gates control residual updates; they do not erase older information already carried by the shortcut. Benefits remain hypotheses.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Recent coherent behavior sometimes reveals specific preferences; recency should not always dominate. (2) Electronics has 12.27% sampled ranking errors and a −0.2595 tenth-percentile margin; these measurements motivate contextual discrimination but cannot establish validation HR@10. (3) Cosine-based collapse scores of 0.5071–0.5234 indicate little average angular alignment, not necessarily healthy dimensional rank. Norm inflation can also enlarge margins without improving rankings [4,5].

**Insights from related work.** (1) NextItNet’s causal dilated residual convolutions provide insertion points for selective update control [1]. (2) DyS4Rec motivates suppressing irrelevant history, without validating this gate [2]. (3) R²NS motivates informative-negative curricula, with false-negative risks [3]. Identity-mapping research further motivates leaving shortcuts untouched [6].

**Framework.** Three directions remain: history selection → residual gates; item identity → jointly learned title/description features; ranking discrimination → curriculum negatives. Each preserves one jointly trained NextItNet per category. The selected gap is context-dependent update control without unavailable compatibility labels, pretrained representations, or independently fitted predictors.

**Candidate assessment.** Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means greater cost. Each score includes a benefit (+) and limitation (−).

| Idea | Assessments |
|---|---|
| Recent-summary residual gate [1,2,6] | O 4: +contextual combination, −standard components; P 6: +adaptive updates, −stale carry persists; U 7: +targets stale and broad matches, −cannot verify fit; M 6: +contextual discrimination, −unproven ranking gain; D 4: +small projection, −causality and controls require care |
| Curriculum multi-negative loss [3] | O 3: +task-focused, −established; P 7: +stronger comparisons, −false negatives; U 5: +specific ranking, −indirect intent modeling; M 8: +separation target, −margin overfitting; D 4: +unchanged backbone, −sampling overhead |
| Joint scratch text residual | O 4: +identity-aware integration, −standard fusion; P 6: +purpose tokens, −sparse supervision; U 7: +specific identity, −missing specifications; M 6: +item discrimination, −text can blur IDs; D 6: +single network, −token pipeline |

**Selected implementation.** Average the latest five nonpadding input embeddings causally, rather than deep states that already contain older history. Gate each complete residual branch immediately before shortcut addition. Use g=2·sigmoid(W[h,summary]+b), W=b=0: initial outputs match the ungated block, although gates can later amplify updates. This replaces bias-three sigmoid initialization, which shrinks updates by 4.74% and reduces gate sensitivity.

Preserve baseline loss and optimizer. Compare ungated, adaptive, fixed-context gate-network, and active capacity controls within the shared budget. Retain four routes, seeds 0/42, at most 200 epochs, 200 batches/epoch, final-nonpadding readout, matching predictor/checkpoint, and diagnostic interfaces. Select by pinned macro validation HR@10; report category hits, paired gains/losses and uncertainty when host outputs permit. Repeated validation selection remains optimistic [7,8]. Add effective-rank and norm diagnostics [5]; margins support interpretation only. No practical compatibility, duplicate-need inference, or full-catalog benefit is established.

idea.description: Add a jointly trained causal recent-embedding-summary gate to each complete corrected NextItNet residual update. Retain one network and one selected checkpoint per category, with untouched identity shortcuts and the existing causal dilated-convolution backbone.
idea.motivation: The proposed mechanism addresses two observed user-facing failures as testable hypotheses: older isolated interactions persisting as current interests, and broadly relevant items outranking specific recent-purpose matches. A gate conditioned on recent item embeddings can modulate history-derived residual updates, but cannot remove older information already present in the carried representation. It also targets contextual positive-negative confusion, especially Electronics’ measured 12.27% sampled wrong-rank rate and negative tenth-percentile margin. It does not establish replacement needs, accessory compatibility, complementarity, or user intent from unavailable evidence. Given 0% research progress, this remains preferable to a larger text pipeline as an initial controlled experiment; curriculum negatives remain a useful subsequent alternative.
idea.implementation_notes:
Architecture: retain the supplied causal dilated convolutions, item_emb, scoring head, objective, optimizer and family-specific sample_batch. Let e be the existing item-ID embedding lookup, masked at padding positions. At each training position t, compute a five-position causal mean of e, dividing by the number of nonpadding entries in that window, clamped to at least one. Using embeddings instead of deep hidden states gives the summary an explicitly local positional support; the block state and residual branch still retain their normal longer receptive fields. For each block, concatenate its current hidden state with this summary, apply a separate channel-wise Linear(2d,d), and set g=2*sigmoid(logit). Multiply the complete baseline residual branch, including its existing convolutions, normalization and activations, by g immediately before adding the untouched shortcut. Reapply the padding mask according to the corrected baseline convention. Do not gate the shortcut or the sum.

Initialization: initialize gate weights and biases to zero, so g=1 and the network initially computes the baseline outputs when shared parameters, dropout draws and computation conventions match. Gate range is (0,2), allowing amplification as well as attenuation; gate-logit derivative at initialization is 0.5. This revises the previous sigmoid bias-three proposal: sigmoid(3)=0.9526 is only approximately baseline-like, shrinks every update by 4.74%, and has derivative 0.04518. Neither construction is an identity-map initialization of the entire block; ReZero's zero residual scaling is a different control. Zero projection weights receive gradients themselves, although they initially block the gate-mediated gradient into its context inputs. Shared item embeddings and hidden states continue receiving gradients through the ordinary backbone paths.

Controls and budget: retain the ungated baseline; compare the adaptive gate against the same gate network receiving fixed zero context, which becomes learned context-independent channel scaling initialized at one. Predeclare a small active-capacity control using a context-free residual bottleneck matched as closely as practical in trainable parameters; specify its width and resulting parameter count before execution. Unused dummy parameters are not a capacity control. A frozen 0.9526 residual-scaling control is relevant only if revisiting the original bias-three gate. Match shared initialization, seed, sampler, training limits and validation schedule across comparisons. Gate variation alone does not demonstrate useful context selection. Run controls sequentially on one GPU as budget allows; do not silently exceed the shared 43,200 GPU-second allowance or average their predictions. If budget prevents controls, report the resulting attribution uncertainty.

Evaluation: retain all four datasets and routing, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per epoch. Preserve the supplied checkpoint-selection schedule and rule rather than introducing extra validation searches. Compare category and macro HR@10 under the pinned host evaluator, with 200 users/category and 99 unique negatives at evaluation seed 42. When host outputs expose per-user indicators, report gained hits, lost hits and paired bootstrap intervals by resampling user pairs within categories; one changed hit is 0.5 percentage points in one category and 0.125 macro percentage points. Respect evaluator tie handling. Do not modify the evaluator to obtain these analyses. Fixed candidates permit paired comparisons but do not establish full-catalog quality, and repeated validation selection makes intervals optimistic.

Diagnostics: preserve log2feats(sequence), item_emb, predict_score(features, items), the host ModelView interfaces, DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Use view.model as the actual trained nn.Module. Retain the B x L loader contract and valid-position masking. Return measured metrics and explicit metric_definitions; do not fabricate unavailable metadata breakdowns. Preserve sampled margins while also reporting score/embedding norm quantiles. Where affordable, compute centered and uncentered spectra separately for nonpadding item embeddings and final-nonpadding sequence features, effective rank with p_i=sigma_i/sum(sigma), top singular-component energy, coordinate variance and near-zero norm fractions on fixed samples. A centered sample of 200 users has rank at most min(d,199). Average cosine alone cannot rule out dimensional collapse; margin growth alone cannot establish ranking improvement. Quantitative probes cannot directly measure current purpose, replacement need or compatibility. Qualitative follow-up uses only the prescribed twenty training users and available item identity evidence; treat those observations as exploratory.

Artifacts and inference: retain DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'] and write artifacts beneath the trial directory. The predictor writer must embed the identical architecture, gate parameterization, pooling width, padding behavior and category routing, and load exactly one selected checkpoint per category. Select the final nonpadding index using the maximum valid positional index, never count-1 for left-padded inputs; retain the supplied empty-history convention. Preserve checkpoint metadata needed to reconstruct the architecture. Do not introduce independent transition/popularity scoring, multiple-checkpoint fusion, pretrained weights, unavailable ratings/reviews/categories, or test access. No execution or validation improvement is claimed.
idea.pseudocode:
CONFIG: window=5; gate=2*sigmoid; gate Linear(2*d,d); initialize its W=b=0.
For each category, initialize one corrected NextItNet using seed 42.
In log2feats(sequence):
    valid = sequence != 0
    e = item_emb(sequence) * valid[..., None]
    summary[t] = sum(e[j] for j=max(0,t-4)..t) / max(1, sum(valid[j] for the same j))
    h = unchanged_baseline_input_processing(sequence)
    for block in baseline_blocks:
        update = block.complete_residual_branch(h)
        gate = 2 * sigmoid(block.gate(concat(h, summary)))
        h = (h + gate * update) * valid[..., None]
    return unchanged_baseline_output_processing(h)
Train with the unchanged baseline loss, optimizer and family-specific sampler.
Preserve 200 batches/epoch, maximum 200 epochs, and the baseline validation/checkpoint schedule.
For prediction:
    features = log2feats(left_padded_sequence)
    last = max(index where sequence[index] != 0)
    scores = predict_score(features[last], candidate_items)
    use supplied baseline convention for empty histories
Generate working/predict.py from the same architecture definition and saved configuration.
Compare ungated, adaptive and predefined controls using host validation only.
Retain one selected checkpoint/category; never combine predictions from controls.

originality.positive: Combines a strictly causal local embedding summary with context-dependent residual-update control inside the required NextItNet family.
originality.negative: Gating, local pooling and baseline-preserving residual modulation are established techniques; this is an incremental architectural hypothesis rather than a demonstrated new model class.

future_potential.positive: Offers a small, interpretable experiment on adaptive history-derived updates and a foundation for controlled studies of contextual discrimination.
future_potential.negative: Untouched shortcuts retain older information, gates may learn static scaling, and improvements on sampled validation candidates may not transfer to full-catalog recommendations.

code_difficulty.positive: Adds one small projection per block without new datasets, pretrained components or independent predictors.
code_difficulty.negative: Faithful branch placement, causal masked pooling, fair controls, diagnostic interpretation and embedded predictor/checkpoint consistency require more care than a simple gate insertion.

related_work.title: NextItNet [1]
contributions: Uses causal dilated residual convolutions for sequential recommendation.
Provides the backbone and residual-update insertion points for the proposed gate.
limitations: Does not establish the proposed recent-summary gate or gains on this benchmark.
Recent deep states can contain older information because stacked convolutions expand receptive fields.

related_work.title: DyS4Rec [2]
contributions: Addresses irrelevant historical interactions obscuring next-interaction intent, according to the supplied search summary.
limitations: Motivates selective history use without verifying this gated NextItNet implementation or benchmark benefit.

related_work.title: R²NS [3]
contributions: Combines uniform-sampling warm-up with informative-negative retrieval and curriculum reranking, according to the supplied search summary.
limitations: Hard negatives can contain relevant unobserved items.
Supports an alternative sampling experiment, not the selected initial gating change.

related_work.title: Understanding Dimensional Collapse in Contrastive Self-supervised Learning [4]
contributions: Studies representation confinement to lower-dimensional subspaces.
Supports distinguishing dimensional collapse from average pairwise angular alignment.
limitations: Does not establish that these NextItNet embeddings are collapsed or that increasing rank improves recommendation.

related_work.title: RankMe [5]
contributions: Uses entropy-based effective rank derived from singular values to characterize learned representations.
limitations: Effective rank depends on sampling, centering and normalization.
Representation rank is a structural diagnostic, not a substitute for validation ranking quality.

related_work.title: Identity Mappings in Deep Residual Networks [6]
contributions: Analyzes the role of identity shortcuts in residual-network signal and gradient propagation.
Motivates applying the proposed gate only to the complete residual branch.
limitations: Does not validate the proposed gate for sequential recommendation.

related_work.title: A Comparison of Statistical Significance Tests for Information Retrieval Evaluation [7]
contributions: Supports paired statistical comparison of retrieval systems on shared evaluation units.
limitations: Paired uncertainty estimates do not account automatically for repeated adaptive validation selection.
Requires access to appropriate per-user host outputs.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation [8]
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can disagree with full-catalog evaluation and can change system ordering.
limitations: Does not justify changing the pinned evaluator; macro validation HR@10 remains the required selection metric.

related_work.title: ReZero is All You Need: Fast Convergence at Large Depth
contributions: Uses zero-initialized residual scaling to initialize residual blocks as identity mappings.
limitations: Identity initialization differs from reproducing the supplied nonzero residual baseline.
An input-independent residual scale does not implement contextual history selection.

related_work.title: Highway Networks
contributions: Introduces gates that control transformed and carried representations.
Clarifies the distinction between controlling residual updates and attenuating carried information.
limitations: Carry gating changes the untouched-shortcut design and is outside the selected minimal experiment.
